currentState: Brask's village-captain politeness to a young foreign mage: 'Miss', as an afterthought; he trusts her through Sylvanas rather than directly. Jaina does not explain the stack to him ('he'd stand there hearing one word in five and wanting his night all the more'); she tells him what to shut and gives him the plain reason. 'I'm sorry, Captain. Every house.'
powerDynamic: Brask has the village; Jaina has the knowledge he lacks. She defers to him in manner ('Thank you, Captain.' in a voice higher than she means) and does not talk down; he defers to her facts via Sylvanas.

physicalDynamics.pattern: He looks past her at the egg stall; she nearly delivers the necromancy speech and shuts her mouth; at the loft he comes up with a torch with his thumb moving on the handle; in the morning she thanks him and he writes her name, asking her to spell Proudmoore.

nameUsage.braskCallsJaina: 'Miss' once; 'the mage' to others; 'The mage. Jaina. Proudmoore.' in his ledger.

history.event: He sends her to Tobin with Dickon.
She tells him to shut the granary and bakehouse and burn every house's flour; he agrees: 'Burn it, then. All of it.'
He had loft boards with her ice carried out and burned; she minds ('the third part had gone on the heap too') but thanks him.

trajectory: One-chapter relationship; ends in mutual obligation; he writes it down.
